items.originalTitle: Max Verstappen slams “unacceptable” bumps at Austin F1 track: “It's out of control”
items.summaryEn: Verstappen said at media day in Austin that the bumps at the Circuit of the Americas are "unacceptable" and that F1 drivers should no longer have to put up with such track conditions.
detailZh: 维斯塔潘批评奥斯汀F1赛道的颠簸“不可接受”：“已经失控了”
维斯塔潘此前开玩笑说，去奥斯汀他需要一根新后背，但现在他称美洲赛道的状况不可接受，并认为F1车手不应再忍受这样的条件。
在新加坡的F1新闻发布会上谈到美国大奖赛时，维斯塔潘立刻开玩笑说，他得订一根新脊椎。这位四届世界冠军关注了9月6日周末在得克萨斯举行的世界耐力锦标赛孤星勒芒站，并表示自己对赛道的状况感到震惊。
尽管维斯塔潘当时还能和安东内利一起拿这件事开玩笑，但他在奥斯汀媒体日明确表示，自己确实担忧“不可接受”的赛道状况。
维斯塔潘表示：“从我在WEC看到的情况来看，赛道颠簸得非常严重。说实话，为了你的脊椎着想，我并不期待那种情况。上一场比赛我还拿这个开玩笑，但说实话，这并不完全是玩笑。我们多年来一直在提这件事，情况实际上已经有点失控了。”
问题源于赛道下方的地面。这条赛道建在得克萨斯州臭名昭著的高塑性黏土上，随着天气条件变化，赛道会遭受严重的胀缩效应。这种持续的移动使赛道极为颠簸，尤其是在沥青承受最大应力的重刹车区。
在2026年比赛之前，部分路段再次进行了重新铺设，包括9号弯到11号弯之间的路段。此外，还进行了维修工作，以处理12号弯到19号弯之间的颠簸。两年前，在2024年美国大奖赛之前，整条赛道都进行了重新铺设。
当Motorsport.com询问维斯塔潘是否认为还需要做更多工作时，这位四届世界冠军强调，赛事组织者不应将场地本身作为借口。
“这非常糟糕。当然，你可以拿土壤问题当借口，但那样的话你早就该知道这一点，并且需要确保对它进行更多加固，”这位荷兰车手说道。
“我的意思是，我喜欢这条赛道，我喜欢这个地方。这是有史以来最好的布局之一，而且我会说，这是最好的场地和最好的城市之一。但对我来说，我们遇到的这些颠簸是不可接受的。
“随着时间的推移，他们在这里那里磨了一点，但你是在给大问题贴膏药，而那只是表面之下的东西。那才是你真正需要首先解决的问题。”
据维斯塔潘称，需要采取影响深远的措施，不仅要关注沥青路面本身，还要关注其下方的土壤。
“但这当然意味着你必须真正把赛道完全开放出来，”他补充道。“这需要花费大量金钱和时间，但说实话，这是摆脱它的唯一办法。因为没错，这些颠簸不是天然的，而且它们已经失控了。”
为什么F1的2026款赛车可能让车手的处境更糟
乍一看，F1不再使用近年来的地面效应赛车似乎因祸得福。毕竟，那些赛车必须调得特别低、特别硬，但当Motorsport.com询问时，维斯塔潘明确表示，2026年的赛车实际上可能让事情更加痛苦。
“可能更糟，因为我们在过弯时离地间隙非常低，”维斯塔潘说。“在直道上你有SM模式，所以会升高。但在大多数地方，尤其是刹车时，你实际上比之前更容易触底。而且大多数颠簸都在刹车区或弯道里，不在真正的直道上。”
“在刹车时，那实际上是一个非常紧张的时刻——尤其是当有这种令人不适的颠簸时，不仅仅是赛道老化带来的颠簸，还有来自下方表面的颠簸，土壤上下移动。有时很难知道会发生什么，或者如果你稍微偏离路线，你不知道那里有什么，因为没有人真正在那里驾驶。所以，是的，这真的很不好。”
所有这些意味着车手的背部承受了相当大的冲击。维斯塔潘表示，他过去几年在COTA已经经历过这种情况。
“例如去年，你在一个弯道中承受大约5-6G的力，但我有一些冲击，垂直载荷，在我的脊柱上超过了9G，”他说。“我可以告诉你，那真的不好玩，尤其是随着年龄增长，你会越来越多地想到这一点。那不是你想要的。”
维斯塔潘补充说，在F1超过11个赛季后，他的脊柱已经不在最佳状态：“我认为有时人们并不真正理解这一点。我可以告诉你，从我做的脊柱检查来看，脊柱的底端看起来并不太好。”
“我知道这是赛车的一部分，我也知道这可能是这项运动的一部分，但这当然也是过去几年我们所用赛车造成的进一步伤害。而现在，如果我们继续认为在这样的情况下驾驶是可以接受的，那么你们将会因此遭受更多痛苦。”
“人们可以说，是啊，但还有更糟糕的运动会对身体某些部位造成伤害。当然，但这就是为什么我不去做那些运动。所以，是的，这并不好。”
detailEn: Max Verstappen slams “unacceptable” bumps at Austin F1 track: “It's out of control”

Verstappen previously joked that he would need a new back for Austin, but he now calls the condition of the Circuit of the Americas unacceptable and believes F1 drivers should no longer have to put up with such conditions

When the United States Grand Prix came up during the Formula 1 press conference in Singapore, Max Verstappen immediately joked that he would have to order a new spine. The four-time world champion had followed the World Endurance Championship round in Texas – The Lone Star Le Mans, held over the weekend of 6 September – and said he was shocked by the condition of the circuit.

Although Verstappen was still able to laugh about it with Kimi Antonelli at the time, he made it clear during the media day in Austin that he is genuinely concerned about the “unacceptable” track conditions.

“From what I saw in WEC, it was extremely badly bumpy. I'm not really looking forward to that, to be honest, for your spine,” said Verstappen. “I was joking about that in the last race, but it's not really a joke to be honest. We mentioned this already for years, that it's actually getting a bit out of control.”

The problem stems from the ground beneath the circuit. Built on Texas’ infamous high-plasticity clay, the track suffers from a severe shrink-swell effect as weather conditions change. This constant shifting leaves the circuit extremely bumpy, particularly in the heavy braking zones where the asphalt is subjected to the greatest stress.

Ahead of the 2026 race, certain sections have been resurfaced again, including the stretch between Turns 9 and 11. In addition, repair work was carried out to address the bumps between Turns 12 and 19. Two years ago, ahead of the 2024 United States Grand Prix, the entire track was resurfaced.
When Motorsport.com asked Verstappen whether he believes more needs to be done, the four-time world champion stressed that the location itself should not be used by the organisers as an excuse.
“It's very bad. Of course, you can use the excuse that the soil is the problem, but then you should have known that and you need to make sure that you reinforce it more,” the Dutchman said.

“I mean, I love this track, I love this place. It's one of the best layouts ever and it's one of the, I would say, best venues and best cities to be at. But for me, the bumps that we have are unacceptable.

“Over time, they've been grinding a little bit here and there, but you're putting a plaster on the big problem and that's just what's underneath. That's what you actually need to tackle in the first place.”
According to Verstappen, far-reaching measures are needed, with attention being paid not only to the tarmac itself, but also to the soil beneath it.

“But that, of course, means you need to really fully open up the track,” he added. “That costs a lot of money and time, but honestly, that's the only way to get rid of it. Because yeah, these bumps are not natural and they are out of control.”
Why F1's 2026 cars could make things even worse for drivers

At first glance, it might seem like a blessing in disguise that F1 no longer uses the ground-effect cars of recent years. After all, those cars had to be run particularly low and stiff, but when asked by Motorsport.com, Verstappen made it clear that the 2026 machinery could actually make things even more painful.

“It's probably worse because we have very low ride heights while cornering,” said Verstappen. “On the straights you have the SM mode, so you go up. But in most places under the braking especially, you actually bottom out more than before. And most of the bumps are under braking or in the corner, not on the actual straight.

“Under braking, it's like actually a very stressful moment – especially when there are these kind of awkward bumps, not just bumps from the track getting older, but bumps from the surface underneath, the soil just moving up and down. Sometimes it's very hard to know what to expect, or if you’re a tiny bit offline, you don't know what is there because no one really drives there. So, yeah, it's really not nice.”
All of this means that drivers' backs take a considerable beating. Verstappen says he has already experienced this at COTA in previous years.

“Last year, for example, you pull around 5-6G in a corner, but I had some impacts, the vertical load, which was like over 9G on my spine,” he said. “I can tell you that it’s really not fun and especially the older you get, you think about that more and more. That's not what you want.”

Verstappen added that his spine is already not in the best possible condition after more than 11 seasons in F1: “I think sometimes people don't really understand that. I can tell you from the checks that I've done from my spine, the bottom end of the spine doesn't look that great.

“I know that's part of racing and I know that can be part of sport, but it's of course also further damage from the cars that we had the last few years. And now if we continue finding this acceptable to drive on, then you are going to suffer from that much more.
“People can say, yeah, but there are worse sports out there for damage to parts of your body. For sure, but that's why I'm not doing them. So, yeah, it's not nice.”

items.summaryZh: 安东内利表示将努力"好好完成这项工作"，他在美国大奖赛迎来首次锁定世界冠军的机会，有望成为F1史上最年轻世界冠军。

items.originalTitle: Kimi Antonelli ready to "finish the job" as first F1 title chance beckons at US GP
items.summaryEn: Antonelli said he will try to "finish the job properly" as he gets his first chance to clinch the world championship at the United States Grand Prix, where he could become F1's youngest-ever world champion.
detailZh: 安东内利在美国大奖赛迎来首个争冠点，准备"完成这项工作"
在本周末的F1美国大奖赛上，安东内利首次获得锁定个人首个世界冠军的机会，尽管可能性不大
F1积分榜大幅领先的安东内利表示，他将努力"好好完成这项工作"，因为他迎来了成为F1史上最年轻世界冠军的首次机会。
这位20岁的车手最早可在本周末美洲赛道举行的美国大奖赛锁定2026年世界冠军，但这一情景需要一些外部因素的帮助。
如果安东内利在周日的比赛中获胜，而落后102分的梅赛德斯队友乔治·拉塞尔获得第九名或更低，并且法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿排名不高于第五，安东内利将赢得总冠军。
当被问及这种可能性时，安东内利誓言他会努力“妥善完成这项工作”，这意味着他会像对待任何其他比赛一样对待奥斯汀-墨西哥-巴西的三连赛。
正是同样的方式让他赢得了八场大奖赛胜利和14次领奖台，使这位意大利车手走到了这一步。
“如果你仔细想想，这确实很疯狂，但这就是为什么我不会去想它，”安东内利说。“对别人来说需要发生灾难性的事情，而对我来说需要是一个完美的周末，这不太可能发生。”
“我们今天早上和博诺（比赛工程师彼得·邦宁顿）开了个会，我们说好就享受比赛，始终保持我全年一贯的心态。
“一场一场来，每个比赛周末都尽力做到最好，然后我们再看。当然，如果我做得好，结果自然会来。”
安东内利承认，夺冠将是童年梦想的实现，也是“不可思议的成就”，但他誓言要先“把这件事好好完成”。
“那会是一个梦想，是我从小就梦想的事情。首先，能让自己处在这样的位置就已经很不可思议了，”他补充道。
“但与此同时，我需要继续前进，继续努力，这还没有结束。首先我们会努力把任务圆满完成，然后我们才能享受剩下的部分。但可以肯定的是，这将是一项了不起的成就。”
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli ready to "finish the job" as first F1 title chance beckons at US GP
At this weekend's Formula 1 United States Grand Prix, Kimi Antonelli gets a first, if unlikely, match point to clinch his maiden world championship
Formula 1’s runaway leader Kimi Antonelli says he will try to "finish the job properly" as he gets a first opportunity to become the series' youngest ever world champion.
The 20-year-old can clinch the 2026 title as early as this weekend's United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas, though this scenario would involve getting some outside help.

Antonelli will win the title if he wins Sunday's race and Mercedes team-mate George Russell - who is 102 points behind - finishes ninth or lower, and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finishes no higher than fifth.
When asked about that possibility, Antonelli vowed he would try to "finish the job properly", which means approaching the Austin-Mexico-Brazil triple-header as he would any other race.
This is the same approach that has netted him the eight grand prix wins and 14 podiums that have got the Italian to this point.

"It definitely is crazy if you think about it, but that's why I won't think about it," Antonelli said. "Something catastrophic to others needs to happen and for me it needs to be a perfect weekend, which is unlikely to happen.
"We had a meeting with Bono [race engineer Peter Bonnington] this morning and we said to just have fun and always have the same mindset as I had all year.
“One race at a time and just try to do the best I can every race weekend and then we'll see. But of course, if I do things well, then the result will come."
Antonelli admitted a title success would be the fulfilment of a childhood dream and an "incredible achievement", but vowed to "finish the job properly" first.
"It would be a dream, it's something I've dreamt of since I was little. First of all to find myself in such a position is incredible," he added.

"But at the same time, I need to keep going, keep pushing and it's not over yet. First we'll try to finish the job properly and then we can enjoy the rest. But for sure, it will be an incredible achievement."

detailZh: 安东内利谈父亲对其F1赛车生涯的担忧
F1积分榜领先者安东内利透露，他的父亲起初反对他的赛车志向
致梅赛德斯车迷。来自银箭车队的最新消息，包括F1新闻、车手动态、赛车研发以及来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃思的赛事分析。
当前F1积分榜领先者安东内利透露，父亲在看到自己因缺钱而结束赛车生涯后，并不希望他成为赛车手。
这位梅赛德斯车手抵达奥斯汀参加美国大奖赛时，在车手积分榜上领先102分，并有可能在周日成为F1历史上最年轻的世界冠军。他的父亲马尔科曾是一名赛车手，如今经营着自己的意大利GT和F4车队，本赛季经常出现在围场中。
在奥斯汀的车手新闻发布会上，当被问及父亲对他帮助有多大，以及他是否真的不希望儿子参赛时，安东内利解释道：“是的，我爸爸就像我的磐石。他和我妈妈以及其他家人一样，是最了解我的人，他知道在某些情况下该如何应对我。
“从小到大，他一直在教我他所知道的一切，首先是关于赛车，但现在他更多地教我关于生活。在比赛期间有像他这样的人陪伴对我非常重要，尤其是在这样重要的一年里。
“他一直在努力平衡自己的工作、他的赛车队以及来观看我的比赛，所以我非常感激他。”
“但在我小时候，甚至一切都还没开始的时候，他并不想让我去赛车，因为这项运动有时非常残酷，尤其是在经济方面，当你没有合适的支持时，这是一项非常艰难的运动。
“我会永远非常感谢梅赛德斯，因为在我很小的时候，他们是唯一愿意在我身上冒险的一方，没有他们，我今天就不会在这里，因为他们是从卡丁车时期一直支持我到现在的那个，也是给我机会的那个。没有他们，我可能不会在这里。
“所以这就是为什么我爸爸不想让我赛车，因为不幸的是，当他自己赛车时，他不得不面对这个现实。他没有任何经济支持，也无法继续他的赛车生涯，所以这就是为什么他创办了自己的赛车队。
“这就是为什么他不想让我赛车，因为他不想让我面对他当年面对过的那种失望，而且因为他很难接受这一点，他只是想保护我。但后来他看到我有热情，所以他决定试一试。”
安东内利目前以340分领跑车手积分榜。他的梅赛德斯队友乔治·拉塞尔以238分位居第二，刘易斯·汉密尔顿以229分排名第三。

detailEn: Kimi Antonelli opens up on father's fears over his F1 racing career
Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli has revealed that his father initially opposed his racing ambitions
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.
Current Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli has revealed that his father did not want him to become a racing driver after seeing his own career end because of a lack of money.

The Mercedes driver arrives in Austin for the United States Grand Prix 102 points clear in the championship and could become the youngest champion in the history of F1 on Sunday. His father, Marco, a former racing driver who now runs his own Italian GT and Formula 4 teams, has been a regular in the paddock this season.

Asked in the drivers' press conference in Austin how much his father had helped him, and whether it was true he had not wanted his son to race, Antonelli explained: "Yes, my dad is like my rock. He's the one, along with my mum and the rest of the family, that knows me best, and he knows how to handle me in certain situations.

"Growing up, he's been teaching me everything he knew, first of all, about racing, but then now he teaches me more about life. It's really important for me to have someone like him during races, especially in such a big year.
"He's been doing an incredible effort on trying to balance his work, his racing team, and coming to my races, so I really appreciate that from him.

"But when I was little, and before everything even started, he didn't want me to race, because the sport can be very cruel at times, and especially financially, it's a very difficult sport when you don't have the right support.

"I will always be very grateful for Mercedes, because they were the one gambling on me when I was very little, and without them, I wouldn't be here today, because they were the one who supported me all the way from karting to now, and they were the one who gave me the opportunities. Without them, I probably wouldn't be here.

"So that's why my dad didn't want me to race, because unfortunately, when he was racing himself, he had to face this reality. He didn't have any financial support, and he couldn't keep on going with his racing career, so that's why he started his own racing team.

"That's why he didn't want me to race, because he didn't want me to face the same kind of disappointments that he had faced back then, and because it was very hard for him to accept it, he just wanted to protect me. But then he saw I had passion, so he decided to give it a go."
Antonelli currently leads the championship with 340 points. His Mercedes team-mate George Russell follows in second with 238 points and Lewis Hamilton is third with 229 points.
The United States Grand Prix will take place from 23-25 October at the Circuit of the Americas.

detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿：法拉利车手在美国大奖赛前解释在新加坡站自行决定策略
法拉利车手首次当面说明，为何在新加坡大奖赛尽管被要求进站，他仍选择不第二次进站；美国大奖赛各节练习与排位将在天空体育F1频道直播，周五晚6点开始第一次练习
刘易斯·汉密尔顿讲述了他无视法拉利策略指令这一代价高昂的决定。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿解释了他为何在新加坡大奖赛无视法拉利的进站指令，他称这是一个自己“已承认”的错误，并将努力不再重犯，但这不会阻止他继续“挑战常规”。
在上一场于滨海湾举行的比赛的最后阶段，汉密尔顿因轮胎磨损严重，加上法拉利维修区指挥墙曾要求他进站、但他最终没有在虚拟安全车期间进站，这一被证明代价高昂的决定让他从领奖台位置跌至第六名。
在这场艰苦的夜间比赛后，他感到身体不适，并获得国际汽联批准免于参加赛后媒体义务；汉密尔顿对自己比赛的唯一评论来自车队发布的一份声明，以及随后他在Instagram上的一则帖子，其中他表示自己对策略失误承担责任。

在奥斯汀周四的新闻发布会上，他首次当面谈到了所发生的事情，当时正值本周末美国大奖赛之前。
在详细的回答中，汉密尔顿首先解释了为什么他最初选择用不同的轮胎——中性胎——起步，而他的队友夏尔·勒克莱尔在他前面一位发车，排在红牛车队杆位得主马克斯·维斯塔潘身后，后者最终赢得了比赛。
“嗯，首先，你从这些经历中学习，”汉密尔顿说道。
“我很少发现自己处于那种位置。当然，接下来的几天感觉不太好，但吃一堑长一智。
“我觉得当我在发车格上列队时，当我知道自己会排在第三位时，我总是在寻找获胜的方法。我总是在考虑做一些可能与众不同的事情。
在F1秀播客中，伯尼·柯林斯探讨了刘易斯·汉密尔顿在新加坡推翻车队策略指令后，是否已经对法拉利失去了信任。
“我本希望采用不同的策略，而不是和查尔斯一样的策略，那样我们只会互相跟随。我们以为马克斯可能会更快，而策略多少显示出我们只是拿到第二和第三，这对我来说还不够。”
“我想要有选择，看看能有什么可能。如果中性胎能撑得更久，也许你可以在比赛中跑得更深，但当我开始跑的时候情况并非如此，而且第一段 stint 感觉并不好。”
“然后显然出来后在查尔斯后面，损失了很多时间，最终，他用的更慢的轮胎，而我一开始用的就是那种，我在软胎上的速度有点类似赞德沃特的情况。”
关于没有听从法拉利在虚拟安全车下进站的召唤、继续跑并接过当时第二名的决定，汉密尔顿说：“我当时正接近维修区入口，我不知道查尔斯要进来，因为我想他最近刚停过，在一瞬间的决定中我决定留在外面。”
“而当我来到维修区旁边时，我意识到这很可能是个错误的决定，但我承认了这一点，承担了责任，然后继续前进。”
在F1秀播客中，伯尼·柯林斯探讨了刘易斯·汉密尔顿在新加坡推翻车队策略指令后，是否已对法拉利失去信任。
“我不会回避这一点”——汉密尔顿将继续“挑战常规”
汉密尔顿表示，自新加坡站以来，车队内部进行了富有成效的讨论，他认为在寻求更好成绩的过程中，自己继续“不断挑战车队和自己”很重要。
他补充道：“我们在幕后进行了良好的对话，讨论如何更好地合作、如何更好地协作，但我认为我们在幕后合作的方式并没有改变。”
“我真心相信，我的工作不是总是随大流，而是不断挑战车队，包括我自己，不断挑战常规。这最终就是我走到今天这一步的原因，我不会回避这一点。”
“有时候事情进展不顺利，那就是其中之一，但你活着就是为了明天继续战斗，作为一个团队，你赢或输。所以我们共同承担重量和代价。”
“当我为车队丢掉积分时，这确实很痛，这不是我经常做的事，但我会努力，我会加倍努力，确保这不会再发生。”

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver explains taking strategy into own hands in Singapore ahead of United States GP

Ferrari driver speaks in person for the first time about why he opted not to pit for a second time in the Singapore GP despite being asked to; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, starting with first practice at 6pm on Friday evening
Lewis Hamilton gives an insight into his costly decision to override Ferrari's strategy call in Singapore.

Lewis Hamilton has explained the reasons why he overrode Ferrari's call to pit in the Singapore Grand Prix, a mistake he says he "owned up to" and will work not to repeat - but which would not prevent him from continuing "challenging the norms".

Hamilton dropped out of the podium positions to sixth on worn tyres in the closing stages of the last race at Marina Bay after what proved the costly decision not to pit under the Virtual Safety Car, as the Ferrari pit wall had requested.

Feeling unwell after the gruelling night race, and being excused from his post-race media obligations by the FIA, Hamilton's only comments about his race came via a statement issued by the team and then a post on his Instagram, in which he said he took responsibility for the strategy going wrong.

He spoke in person about what had happened for the first time in Thursday's press conference in Austin ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

In a detailed answer, Hamilton initially explained why he first chose to start the race on different tyres, the mediums, to team-mate Charles Leclerc who was one place ahead of him on the grid behind Red Bull's polesitting Max Verstappen, the eventual race winner.
"Well, firstly, you learn from these experiences," said Hamilton.
"It's rare that I find myself in that position. Of course, the next couple of days didn't feel so great but you live and you learn.
"I think when I was lining up on grid, when I knew I was going to be third, I'm always looking at ways to win. I'm always looking at doing potentially something different.
On the F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins considers whether Lewis Hamilton has lost trust in Ferrari after overriding a team strategy call in Singapore.

"And I wanted to be on a different strategy, not just the same strategy as Charles, where we just follow each other. We assumed Max would be potentially quicker and the strategy kind of showed just us finishing second and third and that's not enough for me.

"I wanted to have options and see what could be possible. If the medium tyre could last longer, maybe you could go deeper into the race, but it wasn't the case when I got going and it didn't feel great in the first stint.

"Then obviously coming out behind Charles and losing a lot of time, ultimately, with him on the slower tyre, which I was on at the beginning I had the pace on the soft was a bit of a similar scenario to maybe to Zandvoort."

On the decision to not heed Ferrari's call to pit under the Virtual Safety Car and continue on to take over what stood as second place, Hamilton said: "I was coming towards the pit lane entry, and I didn't know Charles was coming in, because I think just recently he had stopped and in a split-second decision I decided to stay out.
"And as soon as I was alongside the pit lane, I realised it's probably the wrong decision, but I owned up to it, took responsibility for it and you move on."
On the F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins considers whether Lewis Hamilton has lost trust in Ferrari after overriding a team strategy call in Singapore.
'I will not shy away from that' - Hamilton to keep 'challenging the norms'

Hamilton said there had been productive discussions in the team since Singapore and that he believed it was important that he continued to "continuously challenge the team, and myself" in the search for better results.

"We've had good conversations in the background of how we can do better together, how we can collaborate better, but I think that nothing's changed in terms of how well we work together in the background," he added.

"I truly believe my job is rather than to follow suit always, it's to continuously challenge the team, and myself including, and just constantly challenging the norms. And that's ultimately how I've got to where I am and I will not shy away from that.
"Sometimes it doesn't go well and that was one of those but you live to fight another day, you win or lose as a team. So we carry the weight and the costs together.
"It definitely hurts when I lose points for the team, it's not something I do very often, but I'll work, I'll double the efforts to make sure that doesn't happen again."

detailZh: '界限被跨越' – 法兰科·科拉平托在针对阿尔派 F1 员工的网络骚扰后公开发声
科拉平托感到有必要录制一段视频信息来向他的粉丝表达。据阿根廷人所说，网络骚扰不仅针对其他 F1 车手，还针对 阿尔派 车队的成员
在 2026 年一级方程式赛季的媒体活动中，法拉利科·科拉平托一直面临着一个反复出现的话题：阿根廷人感到有必要在社交媒体上发声反对骚扰
科拉平托在摩纳哥接受 Motorsport.com 的独家采访时详细讨论了这个问题，以及在此之后许多赛车周末的活动中
上一次新加坡大奖赛之后，然而，阿尔卑斯车手感到有必要更进一步，直接通过视频信息向粉丝群体表达。在许多事情中，他表示感激所有粉丝的支持，但补充说，将仇恨指向他人对他的F1职业生涯毫无帮助。
“首先，我一直非常感激所有支持我的粉丝，”科拉平托在被Motorsport.com问及本周末美国大奖赛前的声明时说。
“但我认为在每一个体育项目和粉丝群体中，都有不好的一面，就是那些发表负面评论、不帮助运动员发挥最佳水平的人。对我来说，最近这已经越过了几条底线。
“我认为可能是最后一件事，就是发表一个我像那样在视频中讲话的声明。这始终会是积极的，所以我非常乐意去做。”
解释他所说的某些界限最近已被跨越的含义时，科拉平托透露，他自己的团队成员也成为了社交媒体上的目标。科拉平托认为这是不可接受的，这促使他再次公开发言。
“特别是我的机械师们受到了很多恶意攻击，”这位23岁的年轻人透露。“我的工程师们也是如此，他们是我团队中希望我表现良好并帮助我发挥的人。我每天都和他们一起工作，看到他们收到这样的信息，这让我感到非常痛苦。”
当被问及这些是团队官方Instagram账号上的评论还是发送给团队成员的个人消息时，科拉平托回答道：“我没有他们的手机，但据我所知，他们收到了信息和评论。再次强调，这对我来说已经越过了界限。”
在实践中，这包括为科拉平托的赛车工作的机械师，他们从一节排位赛到下一节排位赛对赛车的前翼等进行调整。
他们因此被错误地认为是艰难的一节练习的责任者，随后在他们的账户上收到了恶意的消息，尽管Motorsport.com了解阿尔派已经采取了措施来最小化影响。
团队成员被建议保持他们的个人社交媒体账户私密，不要展示任何车队标志，以最小化收到不欢迎消息的风险。
然而，这并没有解决根本问题，这正是科拉平托再次向粉丝发出紧急呼吁的原因。他也强调，这个问题不仅限于F1，而是影响整个社会。
“我可能在过去的10场比赛中都谈到了这个问题，”他说。 “我尽力了，但我认为它一直在跨越一些界限。所以这是我能做的最后一件事，制作一个视频，我认为它有所帮助。”
“你也看到了，Max也是。他也对此发表了评论。这在我们周围发生得很多。这是我们如今在体育界以及生活的许多不同领域面临的问题。艺术家、演员，无处不在。”
“就我个人而言，这并没有对我造成太大的伤害。我不太关注那些评论，我不会太在意。但对一些人来说，这确实[影响了他们]。这就是为什么我们需要关注它。我们需要改进它，希望这个视频能稍微改善一下。”
detailEn: 'Lines were crossed' – Franco Colapinto speaks out after online abuse targeting Alpine F1 staff
Colapinto felt compelled to record a video message addressing his fans. According to the Argentine, the online abuse was directed not only at fellow F1 drivers, but also at Alpine team members
It has become a recurring topic during Franco Colapinto's media sessions throughout the 2026 Formula 1 season: the Argentine feeling the need to speak out against abuse on social media.
Colapinto discussed the issue at length during an exclusive interview with Motorsport.com in Monaco, as well as during many of the race weekends that have followed since.

After the Singapore Grand Prix last time out, however, the Alpine driver felt the urgency to go a step further and address his fanbase directly in a video message. Among other things, he said he appreciated all the support from his fans, but added that directing hate towards others does nothing to help his own F1 career.
“First of all, I've always been very grateful for all the fans supporting me,” said Colapinto, when asked by Motorsport.com about his statement ahead of this weekend’s United States Grand Prix.

“But I think in every sport and fan base, it's got a bad side as well, the hate side of people putting bad comments and not helping athletes perform at their best. To me, it crossed a few lines lately.
“I think it was probably the last thing I could do, to put out a statement of me talking in a video like that. It was always going to be positive, so I was keen to do it.”

Explaining what he meant when he said that certain lines had recently been crossed, Colapinto revealed that even members of his own team had been targeted on social media. Colapinto found that unacceptable, prompting him to speak out once again.

“Especially my mechanics got a lot of hate,” revealed the 23-year-old. “My engineers as well, people from my team that want me to do well and that help me to perform. I'm working with them daily and seeing them getting these kind of messages, it just hurts me in general.”

Asked whether these were comments on the team's official Instagram account or personal messages sent to team members, Colapinto replied: “I don’t have their phones, but from what I understand, they receive messages and comments. Again, it just crossed the line for me.”
In practice, this includes mechanics who work on Colapinto's car and make adjustments to, for example, the front wing from one qualifying segment to the next.

They are then wrongly held responsible for a difficult session and subsequently receive hateful messages on their accounts, although Motorsport.com understands that Alpine has taken measures to minimise the impact.
Team members are advised to keep their personal social media accounts private and not show any team logos, in order to minimise the risk of receiving unwanted messages.

Nevertheless, that does not address the actual problem at its root, which is precisely why Colapinto has once again made an urgent appeal to fans. He also stressed that the problem is not limited to F1, but affects society as a whole.

“I've been talking about this for the last 10 races probably,” he said. “I do my best, but I think it kept crossing some lines. So this was the last thing I could do, making a video, and I think it helped.

“You saw it with Max as well. He also made a statement about it. It's happening a lot around us. It's an issue that we’ve got in sports nowadays, in sports and in many different areas of life. Artists, actors, it's everywhere.

“Personally, it doesn’t hurt me too much. I don't look at those comments too much, I don't put too much attention. But for some it does [affect them]. And that’s why we need to put attention on it. We need to improve it and hopefully this video does improve it slightly.”
